papers.what_it_is: A circuit construction for the exponential of any Pauli string from CNOT, Hadamard and single-qubit rotation gates, built on a permutation-similarity result, then used for first, second and fourth order Suzuki-Trotter simulation of several 1D spin Hamiltonians in Qiskit, with and without noise.

existing.note: The 18-qubit runs cover only the 2-sparse block-diagonal and Ising Hamiltonians, whose terms commute so the Trotter error is zero; the Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising runs go only to 14 qubits. The error is a Frobenius norm distance between unitaries.
existing.value: The authors report that simulations of up to 18 qubits for the 2-sparse block-diagonal and quantum Ising Hamiltonians, and of up to 14 qubits for the other Hamiltonians, show that the error of the proposed circuit simulation closely matches the numerical Trotter approximation error in all cases, the error being the Frobenius norm distance between the exact unitary evolution and the circuit's unitary.

papers.what_it_is: A characterization, by symmetrization over the symmetric group, of the equivariant linear and non-linear maps for geometric QML models on n-node graphs encoded in n qubits, used to unify and extend known invariant and equivariant graph models, with two small numerical studies (graph distinguishability and classical pre-training).

existing.note: The paper adds that the expectation values were assumed exact (no shot noise), that the single-observable model needed 2, 3 or 4 layers, and that the added observables come from the same measurement basis.
existing.value: The authors report that on families of hard-to-distinguish non-isomorphic graphs, a QAOA-encoded model with the single observable of earlier work needs L of 2, 3 or 4 layers to distinguish all pairs, while adding all compatible observables measured in the same basis reduces the circuit to L = 1; they state this does not mean the extended model solves graph isomorphism, since only a very small subset of graphs was considered and expectation values were assumed exact, without shot noise.

assertions.value: The paper defines a map f as equivariant with respect to a group G when f(g · x) = g · f(x) for every g and x, and invariant when f(g · x) = f(x); a parameterized function is equivariant when this holds for arbitrary parameter values.
quotes: We say that a map f : X → Y is equivariant w.r.t. G whenever f (g · x) = g · f (x) (2) for any g ∈ G and any x ∈ X .
The map is said to be invariant whenever f (g · x) = f (x).
Definition 1 is extended to parameterized functions fθ, such as our models or its components (1), when condition (2) hold for arbitrary values of the parameters θ.

papers.what_it_is: A framework that uses the quantum neural tangent kernel at initialization to estimate a QNN's critical learning rate, training decay time and test predictions, derived in the lazy (frozen-kernel) regime and checked in statevector simulations of HEA and HVA models on a TFIM regression dataset, a noisy sinusoid and the Moons dataset.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper, with no simulations or experiments, extending equilibrium propagation to quantum systems by using the variational characterization of the ground state, giving a measurement-based learning rule and illustrating it on the transverse-field Ising model and a quantum harmonic oscillator network.

studying the effect of single measurements of single eigenstates (free or nudge) on the variance of the gradient estimator would be useful

The central idea is to view the cost function C(s, y) as the energy of an interaction between the state variables (s) and desired outputs (y)
termed the 'nudging parameter' that controls the strength of this new interaction

assertions.value: The paper states Theorem 1 (Equilibrium Propagation): the gradient of the cost with respect to the weights equals the β-derivative at zero of the energy's weight derivative at the nudge state, approximated by the finite difference between nudge and free states divided by β; the contrastive rule thus approximates one step of gradient descent; the theorem is proved in Scellier and Bengio (2017).
quotes: The main theoretical result of EP is that the above contrastive learning rule (8) approximates one step of gradient descent on the cost function.
Theorem 1 is proved in Scellier and Bengio [2017].

If the energy term Ek involves only state variables spatially close to wk, the learning rule for wk is local in space.

the learning rule of Eq. (8) yields significantly better results with β < 0 than with β > 0

papers.what_it_is: A classical Monte Carlo estimator over Pauli paths (2MC-OBPPP) for the noise-induced MSE, gradient variance and deviation from a 2-design of parameterized circuits with Pauli-rotation plus Clifford gates under a broad class of non-unital noise (PCS1 channels), with proofs in a long supplement and numerical demonstrations on a hypothetical 435-qubit chip layout.

existing.value: The authors introduce 2MC-OBPPP, a polynomial-time classical estimator of trainability, expressibility and noise robustness for parameterized circuits, and state that, provided the PCS1 channels are O(1)-local, an ε-accurate estimate is obtained at a cost that, for an observable with O(1) Pauli 1-norm and an input state with O(1) non-zero entries, scales linearly in nL times epsilon to the minus fourth with logarithmic factors; computing the noisy expressibility metric additionally requires that the channels' adjoints are PCS1, otherwise only a lower bound is computed.
